transcript.text: Morning, everyone. We've got a situation I need to get resolved before Friday's production run. As you all know, a shipment of 600 drums of moisture-sensitive polyurethane adhesive arrived this morning, but a receiving temperature alarm put the whole shipment on hold. Friday's production schedule is going to need adhesive from this shipment — or an approved replacement — so we can't just let this sit. Before I make a disposition decision, I need to follow our standard huddle process and get findings from each area. Let's hear from quality, maintenance, logistics, and EHS — anything relevant to this hold so we can figure out whether to release this shipment or line up a replacement.

transcript.text: I completed my quality review of the temperature logger this morning. Here's what I found: exactly 72 drums exceeded the approved 8°C exposure limit for 90 minutes, so those 72 drums must remain quarantined per our quality procedure. The remaining 528 drums stayed within specification and are cleared for release. I haven't entered this result into the warehouse hold record yet, but I wanted to share it with the group now so Maya can make her disposition decision with the full picture.
